title: Multi-window, round 3
subtitle: Decision walkthrough · 2 Nov 2026 · narrated by Duo's house voice
posterLine: What the research found, then six decisions. Tap play and listen; it stops when it needs you.
footer: Built with the decision-walkthrough skill from docs/research/multi-window-walkthrough/spec.json. Answers are saved in this page and sent to director-duo-v2.

lines.text: This is the multi-window research, round three, and it ends in six decisions.
A power user on v1 works in several windows, one per project, and switches between them all day.
Back in October you chose independent windows, in DL-141.
Nothing else has been decided since, so this round reads today's code and asks how to build it small.

chapters.title: One core, a model per window

lines.text: The good news is in the code. Duo's main model already describes itself as one instance per window.
Its state comes in three kinds.
App-wide things, like sessions, terminals and search, move into a new core that exists once.
Per-project memory, like tabs and shells, lives in the core too, keyed by project, so it follows the project to any window.
Per-window things, like the view, the split and the editors, stay on the model.
So a second window is just a second model over the same core.
That gives a plan in small slices.
Slice zero makes the cut with nothing visible changing, in about two build sessions.
Slice one is what the power user needs. New Window, Open in New Window, and each window titled with its project, in one or two sessions.
Slice two brings the window set back after a relaunch. Your window colours get a slice of their own, and pins wait for later.
v1 spent thirteen to seventeen engineer-weeks on this. Slices zero and one here are three or four sessions, because of one rule.

chapters.title: Settled: a project lives in one window

lines.text: That rule is the one you settled earlier today, in DL-308.
If a project is already open in another window, opening it again brings that window forward, the way Xcode and Zed do it.
So a session's terminal only ever has one window to be in, which keeps the first slices simple.

chapters.title: When to build
chapters.why: The build plan (§3a) puts multi-window after v1. Building now logs the power user as the reason.

lines.text: First decision. When to build it.
The build plan puts multi-window after v1, so building it now means logging why, and the reason is the power user.
I recommend slices zero and one now, then slice two.

options.label: Slices 0 and 1 now, then slice 2
options.desc: Logged past §3a for the power user. Restore and needs-you follow.

lines.text: Option one. Slices zero and one now, three or four sessions, then restore and needs-you follow.

options.label: Slices 0, 1 and 2 now
options.desc: The window set survives relaunch from the start. About one more session.

lines.text: Option two adds slice two up front, so the window set survives a relaunch from the start. About one more session.

options.label: Slice 0 only for now
options.desc: The plumbing, with no visible change. Windows wait.

lines.text: Option three builds only the core. Nothing changes on screen, and windows wait.
Option four leaves it all until after v1, as the plan says today.

chapters.title: What slice 1 includes
chapters.why: The smallest thing that lets the power user switch projects in two windows.

look.label: Board 1 · How a new window opens

lines.text: Next, what slice one includes.
I'd keep it to windows. New Window on ⌥⌘N, and Open in New Window on a project's right-click menu.
Each window is titled with its project, and the system's Window menu and ⌘` move between them.

options.label: New Window, Open in New Window, titles, the system Window menu
options.desc: Board 1's option A. No pin, no colour.

lines.text: Option one is just that, board one's option A. No pin, and no colour.

options.label: Also Pin (board 2)
options.desc: Needs Q-95's D2 and D3 answered first.

lines.text: Option two adds Pin, from board two. It needs the pinning questions answered first.

options.label: Also window colours (boards 4a to 4c)
options.desc: Needs Q-435 first. About one more session.

lines.text: Option three adds window colours, about one more session, once the colour questions are settled.

chapters.title: Home with several windows
chapters.ask: What does a second window show in Home's pane?
chapters.why: Home has one terminal, and it can be live in only one window.

lines.text: Home has one terminal, and a terminal can only be live in one window.
So what does a second window show in Home's pane?

options.label: All projects in every window; Home live in one, Show Here in the others
options.desc: Board 10's stand-in. Chat there can come later with Q-98's D10.

lines.text: I recommend every window keeps All projects. Home is live in the window that last had it, and the others say so, with a Show Here button.

options.label: All projects only in the first window
options.desc: Other windows hold one project each.

lines.text: Or only the first window gets All projects, and every other window holds one project.

options.label: Home's chat in every window now
options.desc: Board 10's chat option, with a composer focus check per window. About half a slice more.

lines.text: Or every window gets Home's chat now, which is about half a slice more.

chapters.title: Window colours: the palette
chapters.why: Your idea, from your note on Q-99 (ENH-319). Board 4a has every value, light and dark.

look.label: Board 4a · A base colour for each window, light and dark

chapters.hint: Tap a swatch, or Light / Dark

lines.text: Now the window colours. This one's your idea, from your note on Q-99, a base colour for each window to help you switch context.
The toolbar takes the colour, and the side panes a lighter shade.
The console, the text, the document and the needs-you orange never change.
It works in dark too, and every text colour still passes four and a half to one.

options.label: Sky, Sage, Lilac, Sand and None, as drawn
options.desc: Light and dark values with their contrast on board 4a.

lines.text: Option one is the palette as drawn. Sky, Sage, Lilac, Sand, and None.

options.label: More colours
options.desc: Say which in the comment. None may be orange or red.

lines.text: Option two asks for more colours. Say which in the comment, as long as none is orange or red.

options.label: Redraw them
options.desc: Say what's off in the comment.

lines.text: Option three is a redraw, if these feel off. Say what's off in the comment.

chapters.title: Window colours: a new window's colour
chapters.ask: What colour does a new window get?
chapters.why: To change any window's colour: the swatch after the project's name, Window › Window Colour, or duo2 window colour.

look.label: Board 4b · A new window's colour, and changing it

lines.text: What colour does a new window get?
Your first window stays None, so Duo looks as it does today until you open a second.

options.label: The next colour no open window has
options.desc: Sky, Sage, Lilac, Sand, then round again. A switch in the swatch's menu turns it off.

lines.text: I recommend each new window takes the next colour no open window has. Sky, Sage, Lilac, Sand, then round again. A switch turns it off.

options.label: New windows open plain; you pick

lines.text: Or new windows open plain, and you pick a colour from the swatch after the project's name.

chapters.title: Window colours and Classic
chapters.why: Classic (DL-252) repaints the same grounds for the whole app, so the two can't be on together.

lines.text: Last one. Classic repaints the same grounds for the whole app, so it can't be on alongside window colours.
One of them has to give way.

options.label: Classic turns window colours off
options.desc: Every window goes Classic; each gets its colour back when you leave Classic.

lines.text: I recommend Classic takes over. Every window turns Classic, and each one gets its colour back when you leave it.

options.label: Window colours make Classic unavailable
options.desc: Classic is dimmed until every window is None.

lines.text: Or window colours win, and Classic stays dimmed in Settings until every window is None.
That's all six.
Each answer went to the director as you saved it, and Copy decisions puts them all on the clipboard, for any Claude.
Q-426 and Q-427, from the power-user audit, stay on the old review page.
